text: Husserl's epoché (the phenomenological reduction) consists in:
choices: Denying that the external world exists (metaphysical idealism)
Bracketing or suspending the natural attitude's assumption of the world's independent existence
Inferring the existence of other minds by analogy
explanation: The epoché brackets or suspends the natural attitude's tacit commitment to the world's independent existence so that we can describe how things appear to consciousness. It is explicitly not a denial that the world exists (Husserl is not thereby an idealist), not a reduction to neuroscience, and not an inference to other minds.
